summary: Bumps the exact pin on @cipherstash/protect-ffi from 0.30.0 to 0.31.0 in @cipherstash/stack (runtime dependency, so it reaches every consumer) and adapts to its breaking changes: the ProtectError class is replaced by a value-based isProtectErrorCode guard, the WASM newClient takes credentials under clientOpts and the strategy under authStrategy, WASM encryptConfig is no longer pre-normalised, and the undeclared correlation `id` is stripped from every bulk payload because 0.31 rejects unknown keys. The most material release risk is intended and loud: an explicitly supplied base64 clientKey now fails at client construction, which the change handles with a major changeset, skill documentation and a CI pre-flight. The item a reviewer should resolve is that the native entry still passes the strategy under the deprecated `strategy` name while the WASM entry was moved to `authStrategy`; if that alias is not honoured by the native binding, a caller's authStrategy would be dropped. All 16 CI checks passed, including credentialed integration and WASM Deno E2E jobs, which supports the bulk-payload and cast_as changes against the real 0.31 binary. I searched every native and WASM FFI call site at head and found no remaining undeclared payload keys.

behaviour_changes.description: @cipherstash/stack's runtime dependency on @cipherstash/protect-ffi moves from 0.30.0 to 0.31.0 (exact pin), so every consumer of stack gets the new native and WASM bindings on upgrade; the drizzle and supabase adapters change only their devDependency.

An explicitly supplied clientKey (config.clientKey or CS_CLIENT_KEY) must now be hex. Under 0.30 base64 was also accepted; under 0.31 it is rejected at client construction. This is a protect-ffi behaviour reported in the changeset and PR, not code in this diff; the change documents it and marks stack major.

WASM entry newClient now receives authStrategy (was strategy), credentials nested under clientOpts (were top level), the encryptConfig without normalizeCastAs, and no `as never` cast. The native entry's newClient call is unchanged and still passes `strategy:`.

Bulk encrypt/decrypt payloads (bulk-encrypt, bulk-decrypt and all eight model-helper call sites) no longer forward the correlation `id` to the FFI. Result correlation stays positional via the original array / keyMap.

getErrorCode and the DynamoDB handleError now classify an error by whether its `code` value is a known protect-ffi code, instead of `instanceof ProtectError`. DynamoDB errors whose code is any other string (e.g. ECONNRESET) now report DYNAMODB_ENCRYPTION_ERROR rather than passing the foreign code through.
The require-cs-secrets composite action gains a step that fails a credentialed CI job when CS_CLIENT_KEY is not even-length hex. It never echoes the key.
The bundled stash-auth agent skill (shipped to customer repositories) gains guidance that CS_CLIENT_KEY must be hex, with a recovery path that differs between the native and wasm-inline entries.

failure_scenarios.title: Deployments with a base64 clientKey fail at client construction after upgrading
failure_scenarios.trigger: A customer upgrades @cipherstash/stack with CS_CLIENT_KEY or config.clientKey holding the base64 form (e.g. copied from ~/.cipherstash/secretkey.json).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: stack pins protect-ffi exactly, so the upgrade forces 0.31.0, whose clientKey decoder is reported to be hex-only. The error message deliberately omits detail. On wasm-inline there is no profile-store fallback; clientId/clientKey are required config.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Every encryption and decryption operation in the affected service fails from startup until the key is re-encoded. The failure is loud and recoverable without data loss, but it is a full outage of the encryption path for that service.

existing_verification.description: Credentialed CI jobs passed on head, behind the new hex pre-flight, showing a hex key constructs and operates on 0.31.0.

missing_verification: No test asserts the base64 rejection or its error message (the behaviour lives in protect-ffi, whose source was unavailable).
Number of customers supplying base64 keys is unknown.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Already mitigated by a major version bump, changeset upgrade notes and the stash-auth skill. Make sure the release notes put the hex requirement first. Consider a stack-side pre-construction check that names encoding as the likely cause without echoing the key.

failure_scenarios.title: Native entry still passes `strategy`; a supplied authStrategy could be dropped by 0.31
failure_scenarios.trigger: A caller passes config.authStrategy (e.g. OidcFederationStrategy) to the native Encryption client, and the 0.31 native binding does not honour the deprecated `strategy` name.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The same change renames strategy to authStrategy on the WASM entry because 0.31 renamed the field. Its own test comments say `strategy` 'still works there as a deprecated alias' and is 'slated for removal'. The native call at encryption/index.ts:143 still sends `strategy: config.authStrategy`. The PR states that both entries now deserialize the same NewClientOptions. If the alias is not honoured now, or is removed in a later protect-ffi bump, the client falls back to the default auto strategy using env credentials.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Without lock context, operations could run under the service's ambient credentials instead of the caller's federated identity. With lock context, operations would fail. This is an identity-binding change on the auth path.

existing_verification.description: init-strategy.test.ts asserts that the strategy reaches a MOCKED newClient as opts.strategy. It cannot show that the real 0.31 binding honours the name.

matrix-identity.integration.test.ts passes authStrategy to the native client live. The Drizzle integration job that globs it passed, but the suite skips without CLERK_MACHINE_TOKEN, and job-level results cannot show whether it ran.

missing_verification: Confirmation, from 0.31.0's native NewClientOptions declaration or a live run, that `strategy` is honoured on the native binding.
A non-mocked test that a native client built with authStrategy actually calls the strategy's getToken().
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Pass `authStrategy: config.authStrategy` on the native entry as well, matching the WASM change, and update init-strategy.test.ts. Alternatively, confirm the alias against the 0.31.0 typings and Rust deserializer before release.

failure_scenarios.title: WASM encryptConfig no longer pre-normalised; a cast mapped differently by 0.31 would change column semantics
failure_scenarios.trigger: A WASM-entry schema uses an SDK cast_as variant that 0.31's Rust-side normalisation maps differently from stack's toEqlCastAs, or does not accept.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: normalizeCastAs was removed from the newClient path (it is kept only as deprecated). The SDK spelling now reaches protect-ffi, which is reported to normalise on both bindings. The native entry already relied on FFI normalisation before this change, so the WASM entry now converges on native behaviour.
failure_scenarios.consequence: The likely failure is loud: client construction fails for that column type. If the mapping differed silently, values could be encrypted with a different plaintext cast than native clients use for the same column. Query terms could then fail to match or values could decode as the wrong type across entries.

failure_scenarios.title: Callers branching on DynamoDB error.code stop matching transport errors
failure_scenarios.trigger: A consumer's retry or alerting logic keys off EncryptedDynamoDBError.code values such as ECONNRESET.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: handleError now returns the code only if isProtectErrorCode accepts it; otherwise DYNAMODB_ENCRYPTION_ERROR.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Retries on transient network faults stop firing, or errors are categorised differently in monitoring. The change is intentional, documented in the changeset and reversible by the caller.

evidence.claim: @cipherstash/protect-ffi pinned exactly to 0.31.0 as a runtime dependency of @cipherstash/stack.
Collector reports protect-ffi 0.30.0 -> 0.31.0 in stack dependencies and in the drizzle/supabase devDependencies.
The PR describes the new hex-only clientKey and a CI pre-flight added because a base64 secret makes all credentialed workflows fail with a message that never mentions encoding.
Major changeset: clientKey must be hex and base64 is rejected at construction; DynamoDB error codes are now checked against the known set; bulk ops no longer forward the id.
The bundled skill says CS_CLIENT_KEY must be hex and that wasm-inline has no profile-store fallback.

WASM newClient now passes authStrategy, clientOpts {clientId, clientKey}, an unnormalised encryptConfig and eqlVersion 3. Comments say keyset at top level would be silently ignored, and that 0.31 renamed strategy to authStrategy.
The native newClient call (unchanged by this diff) passes `strategy: config.authStrategy`, with credentials and keyset under clientOpts.
withoutId strips `id` from bulk payloads and is applied at all eight encryptBulk/decryptBulk call sites; results are correlated by index via keyMap.
createEncryptPayloads no longer includes id.
createDecryptPayloads no longer includes id.
getErrorCode returns a code only when isProtectErrorCode accepts its value.
handleError uses isProtectErrorCode, otherwise DYNAMODB_ENCRYPTION_ERROR; previously any string code was passed through.
The new step fails the job unless CS_CLIENT_KEY matches ^[0-9a-fA-F]+$ with even length; it prints only the length.
tests.yml (and the integration workflows) call require-cs-secrets with secrets.CS_CLIENT_KEY.
All 16 check runs on the head commit succeeded, including Run Tests (Node 22/24, Bun), Run E2E Tests, Run WASM E2E Tests (Deno), Drizzle/Supabase/prisma-next v3 integration and Lint.
The test comment says `strategy` still works as a deprecated alias slated for removal, and asserts the WASM call uses authStrategy with no strategy field.
With protect-ffi mocked, the test asserts the native client forwards the strategy as opts.strategy.
The live native-client identity suite uses config.authStrategy with OidcFederationStrategy and skips when CLERK_MACHINE_TOKEN is unset.
The mocked-FFI test now expects cast_as 'string' to reach newClient unnormalised.
The new handleError tests cover ECONNRESET mapping to DYNAMODB_ENCRYPTION_ERROR, UNKNOWN_COLUMN being preserved, and missing or non-string codes.
